gap.cards[0].description: A marketplace operates because users trust the platform enough to transact with strangers. That trust is built incrementally and lost at scale. A single cluster of fake sellers, a coordinated review manipulation, or a refund fraud ring damages platform credibility far beyond the direct financial loss.
gap.cards[0].image.alt: Trust is infrastructure, not a feature
gap.cards[0].title: Trust is infrastructure, not a feature
gap.cards[1].description: Banks run KYC. Lenders pull bureau scores. Marketplaces often operate with a phone number, an email, and a self-declared profile. The intelligence available at the point of a platform decision is structurally thinner than what regulated institutions require for equivalent risk exposure.
gap.cards[1].image.alt: Less known about the user than any other financial relationship
gap.cards[1].title: Less known about the user than any other financial relationship
gap.cards[2].description: Referral programmes, sign-up incentives, and cashback offers are systematically targeted by coordinated networks. These programmes are designed to acquire genuine users. They disproportionately attract organised exploitation, converting acquisition spend into fraud loss at scale.
gap.cards[2].image.alt: Growth spend as an attack surface
gap.cards[2].title: Growth spend as an attack surface
gap.cards[3].description: Trust and safety operations designed for thousands of users cannot sustain millions. Investigation queues grow faster than headcount. Individual account review misses coordinated patterns that are only visible across the network.
gap.cards[3].image.alt: Manual review doesn't survive platform scale
gap.cards[3].title: Manual review doesn't survive platform scale
